messages:
Aisha (eng): quick q — I'm debugging a memory spike on the prod task-runner. Is it OK to run a short tcpdump/pkt capture for ~2min? worried about sensitive headers/bodies ending up in pcaps. pinging @Tom and @Lee for guidance.

Tom (oncall): ok to capture, but follow the prod-debug runbook rules. get JIT bastion access first, and truncate packets to avoid bodies. also: name the file with the incident id and mark as 'sensitive' in S3.

Aisha (eng): thanks. what's the recommended truncation size and upload flow? should I mask IPs before uploading?

Lee (security): do NOT upload raw pcaps that contain payloads. preferred pattern: truncate captures to headers only, keep local copies deleted after upload, and request approval in the incident thread if you need an exception. see runbook -> "Prod Debug Safety" section 3.1.1.

Lee (security): suggested quick steps: 1) request JIT access via ops-bastion-bot (reason = "investigate memory spike"), 2) on the host run a truncated capture, 3) inspect locally, 4) if you must share, scrub PII/auth and upload to encrypted S3 with lifecycle 30d and tag = "sensitive:pcap".

Tom (oncall): example truncation command we use for quick header-only captures: 
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 96 -w /tmp/prod-INC1839-trunc.pcap 'tcp and (port 80 or port 443 or host 10.2.3.4)'
```
This keeps packet headers (96 bytes) and avoids most bodies. adjust host/port filters to narrow scope.

Lee (security): additional checks: - don't capture logs that include Authorization headers. If you're troubleshooting HTTP, prefer app-level logs with redaction hooks. If you must capture TLS traffic, only capture metadata (IP/port/ssl state), not decrypted payloads.

Aisha (eng): got it. after capture, what's the scrub step? any approved tools?

Lee (security): approved flow for sharing: 1) truncate with -s, 2) inspect locally, 3) run a metadata-only export or use a scrubbing tool (e.g., internal pcap-scrub; if unavailable, keep only pcap name and timestamps), 4) upload to s3://redwood-secured/incident-logs/INC1839/ with encryption and tag as noted. Delete /tmp copy immediately and confirm deletion in thread.

ops-bastion-bot: JIT access request received for Aisha (eng). Approval needed from oncall (Tom). Reply `approve` or `deny`.

Tom (oncall): approved for 15 minutes. Beaconing rules apply. Remember to run from the bastion and not from a developer laptop.

Aisha (eng): thanks, I have JIT and will run the truncated capture now. I'll follow the upload + deletion steps and post a short summary here.

Lee (security): one last reminder — if you see tokens/credentials in any capture, stop and notify security@redwood immediately.

Aisha (eng): understood. will escalate if I find creds. :thumbsup:
